title: Building a Good Name: Or the Family Name as Inheritance
author: Foster, Michael
summary: A family name is an inheritance that carries weight and meaning. It represents not just lineage but the accumulated reputation and character of the family that bears it. Parents bear responsibility for stewarding the family name—maintaining standards, teaching their children to uphold the family honor, and ensuring the name is passed on with integrity. In modern culture, the family name has lost significance; it is viewed as merely a label rather than a trust. Yet teaching children to care about their family name teaches them that they are part of something larger than themselves, that their actions affect others, and that reputation and honor matter. A good name is worth more than wealth.
points: A family name represents inherited reputation and character, not just genealogy.
Parents must teach children that they are stewards of the family name, responsible for upholding it.
The loss of family name significance in modern culture reflects broader loss of inherited identity and responsibility.
Teaching children to value their family name teaches them honor and connection to something beyond themselves.
quotes: A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches.
Your family name is an inheritance—carry it with care and integrity.
Children should understand they are part of a family legacy, and their actions affect that legacy.” Archived from We Made People Substack on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
